learningGoals: Find HCF of two numbers under 50 by inspection in under 10 seconds

coreIdeas: HCF is the greatest factor common to all given numbers; spot it by listing factors quickly
LCM is the smallest multiple shared by all given numbers; build it from highest prime powers
The identity a × b = HCF(a,b) × LCM(a,b) lets you find one if you know the other

sessionFlow.coachHook: Look at 24 and 36 — they share factors. The biggest one they share is the HCF. Can you see it?
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: HCF means the biggest number that divides all the given numbers exactly.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Superb! 6 is the biggest factor shared by 18 and 30!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: List factors of 18 and 30 separately, then spot the common ones.

exercises.hint: List all factors of 18 and 30, then find the largest common one.
List factors of both numbers and find the largest common one.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Prime factorisation is the Vedic shortcut to cracking any HCF. Break each number into its prime building blocks!

boardDemo.title: Prime Factorisation of 36 and 48
steps: HCF: take lowest power of each common prime → 2² × 3 = 12

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Break each number into primes, then take the lowest power of each prime that appears in both.
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: 60 written as a product of primes = ?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Start dividing 60 by 2 repeatedly, then try 3, then 5.

exercises.questionText: Write 60 as a product of prime factors.
Which is the correct prime factorisation of 72?

sessionFlow.coachHook: LCM is like finding the smallest meeting point for two number trains on the track. Use highest prime powers!

boardDemo.title: LCM(12, 18)
steps: For LCM: take HIGHEST power of each prime

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: LCM uses the highest power of every prime that appears in any of the numbers.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! LCM(4,6) = 12. Both 4 and 6 divide into 12 evenly!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: 4 = 2², 6 = 2×3. Take highest powers: 2² and 3. Multiply them.

exercises.hint: 4 = 2², 6 = 2 × 3. Take highest powers of all primes.

sessionFlow.subtopic: HCF × LCM = Product of Two Numbers
sessionFlow.coachHook: Here's a Vedic shortcut: HCF × LCM always equals a × b. Know one, find the other instantly!
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: For any two numbers: HCF × LCM = first number × second number.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: HCF of two numbers is 6 and their product is 216. Find their LCM.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! LCM = 36. The identity works like a charm!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Use the formula: LCM = product ÷ HCF = 216 ÷ 6.

exercises.questionText: The HCF of two numbers is 6 and their product is 216. Find their LCM.
Two numbers have HCF = 4 and LCM = 48. What is their product?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Quick HCF or LCM — MCQ Drill
sessionFlow.coachHook: No pencil needed — train your brain to see HCF and LCM at a glance. Go!

boardDemo.title: Mental HCF/LCM Tips
steps: If one number divides the other, HCF = smaller number
If numbers share no common factors, HCF = 1
LCM of co-prime numbers = their product

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: If a divides b evenly, HCF(a,b) = a and LCM(a,b) = b.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: What is HCF(12, 36) — can you see it without writing?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Does 12 go into 36? Yes! So 12 is already the HCF.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: 36 ÷ 12 = 3 exactly, so 12 is a factor of 36, making HCF = 12.

exercises.hint: 5 and 7 share no common factors (they are co-prime).

sessionFlow.subtopic: Fill-the-Step: HCF and LCM of 48 and 72
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's prove HCF(48,72)=24 and LCM(48,72)=144 together, one step at a time!

boardDemo.title: HCF and LCM of 48, 72 — Full Working

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: For HCF take lowest powers; for LCM take highest powers of all prime factors.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Fill in the blanks to find HCF and LCM of 48 and 72.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! HCF = 24 and LCM = 144. The identity holds: 48×72 = 24×144!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: For HCF pick lowest powers of each prime; for LCM pick highest powers.

exercises.questionText: Find HCF and LCM of 48 and 72 step by step.

steps.label: HCF (lowest powers)
steps.hint: Min power of 2 is 3, min power of 3 is 1: 2³×3 = 24

steps.label: LCM (highest powers)
steps.hint: Max power of 2 is 4, max power of 3 is 2: 2⁴×3² = 144

sessionFlow.subtopic: Word Problems — Rows and Common Multiples
sessionFlow.coachHook: Vedic teachers used HCF and LCM for everyday arrangements — tiling floors, arranging armies in rows. Let's try!

boardDemo.title: Word Problem: Arranging Items in Equal Rows
steps: Problem: 36 apples and 48 oranges arranged in equal rows, no fruit mixed. Max row size?

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: When we need the largest group size with no remainder, we use HCF. For smallest shared repeat, we use LCM.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Bells ring every 8 minutes and 12 minutes. When do they next ring together?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! They ring together after 24 minutes. LCM = 24!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: LCM(8, 12) = 24. Bells ring together every 24 minutes.

exercises.questionText: Two bells ring every 8 minutes and 12 minutes. After how many minutes will they ring together?

visual.caption: Number line showing multiples of 8 and 12 meeting at 24

exercises.questionText: 36 mangoes and 48 bananas are to be packed in equal boxes with no fruit mixed. What is the maximum number of fruits per box?

sessionFlow.coachHook: You've got the tools. Now build the speed! Solve all 5 pairs as fast as you can!

boardDemo.title: Speed Tips
steps: If one number is a multiple of the other: HCF = smaller, LCM = larger
Always cross-check: HCF × LCM = product of numbers

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Speed and accuracy together — that is the Vedic way!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Lightning fast! You are a Vedic Speed Factor Master!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Take each pair one at a time. Use prime factorisation if needed.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Think you can handle HCF of THREE numbers at once? The Vedic method scales up perfectly!

boardDemo.title: HCF(36, 48, 60)
steps: Common primes in ALL three: 2 and 3

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: For HCF of three numbers, take primes common to ALL three and use the lowest power each time.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Find HCF(36, 48, 60) on your own now.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! HCF = 12. You've mastered the three-number challenge!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Find prime factorisations of all three, then take lowest powers of common primes only.

exercises.hint: Factorise all three, then take the lowest power of each prime common to all.
